html:
The War of the Spanish Succession was a European war of 1701 to 1714 over who should inherit the throne of Spain and its huge empire.

In 1700 the Spanish king Charles II died without children and left everything to Philip of Anjou, a grandson of Louis XIV of France. The other powers feared a union of France and Spain. The Grand Alliance of England (Britain after 1707), the Dutch Republic and the Austrian Habsburgs backed the Habsburg Archduke Charles instead. The Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy beat the French at Blenheim in 1704 and in later battles, while Spain itself split in a civil war: Castile stood by Philip, the lands of Aragon and Catalonia by Charles.

When Charles became emperor in 1711, Britain lost interest in making him king of Spain too, and peace was made at Utrecht in 1713 and Rastatt in 1714:

  • Philip V kept Spain and its American empire but gave up any claim to France.
  • The Austrian Habsburgs took the Spanish Netherlands, Milan, Naples and Sardinia, the base of the later Austrian power in Italy.
  • Savoy got Sicily and a royal crown.
  • Britain got Gibraltar and Minorca, land in North America from France, and the right to sell enslaved Africans in Spanish America.

Philip then ended the separate laws of Aragon and Catalonia, making Spain a more centralised state.
sum: The War of the Spanish Succession was a European war of 1701 to 1714 over who should inherit the throne of Spain and its huge empire.
